BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review Memo
**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) – departures from Buyer Playbook

---

## 0. Preliminary point: the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" should be disregarded

The Seller's package contains a note asserting that clauses marked [STANDARD] "have been reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that "the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." That is not correct on our record:

- Nothing in our playbook records agreement to any of these positions. Our authority instructions are explicit that the 20% cap and 18-month period require written approval from Amelia Frost, and none has been given.
- The Seller cannot unilaterally re-label its own proposals as "cleared" to narrow our review. The [STANDARD] tags are the Seller's characterisation of the other side's draft, not a record of agreement.
- Nearly every clause tagged [STANDARD] is in fact a departure from our playbook — which is precisely why the tagging matters.

**Recommendation:** Respond in writing that no clause is agreed, that all tags are rejected, and that the Buyer's mark-up addresses the full package. Do not let the "[OPEN] only" framing filter into our internal issues list or any Steering Committee paper.

---

## 1. Liability regime (Clauses 12.1 – 12.3, 13)

| Item | Seller draft | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m opening; 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority | **Reject.** The Seller has pitched straight to our fallback. We have no authority to accept it. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. |
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject** – 5x our position. |
| Basket | AUD 250,000, **excess-only** | AUD 50,000, **first-dollar** | **Reject on both axes.** The basket is 5x ours and the switch to a deductible rather than a tipping basket is a substantive value transfer (AUD 250k deducted from every recovery). |
| Claims period | 18 months | 24 months; 18 months needs Amelia Frost approval (not given) | **Reject.** Counter at 24 months. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Blanket default | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** This is the mechanism by which the general regime quietly swallows the fundamental, tax, IP and indemnity categories. Reverse the default: limitations apply only to the category to which they are expressly stated to apply. |

**Reasoning:** Combined, the Seller's package (low cap + high deductible basket + short period + default spill-over of limitations) materially erodes warranty protection on a AUD 24m deal. Each element is individually off-playbook; together they are well outside the negotiating envelope we have authority for.

---

## 2. Fundamental / Title warranties

**Seller:** capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."

**Playbook:** separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.

**Assessment: Reject outright.** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title recourse at 20% of price and to let it lapse after 18 months. If we do not own the shares, we need the full price back. This is a non-negotiable structural point, not a pricing point. It also interacts with the Clause 12.3 default rule (Item 1) and Clause 9.3/12.8/20.5 (Item 3): all three must be fixed together or any one of them reintroduces the problem.

---

## 3. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)

**Playbook:** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; no one may waive this.

**Assessment: Reject.** As drafted, there is no fraud carve-out at all. "Claims of any nature" would on its face purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims and to apply non-reliance against fraudulent misrepresentation. Apart from being unacceptable commercially, such a provision is of doubtful enforceability and invites a dispute later. Insert an express, unwaivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct across Clauses 9.3, 12, 13 and 20.5, and expressly exclude the specific indemnities (Ironquay, bonuses, Riverlark, incident) and fundamental warranties from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language.

---

## 4. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2)

**Seller:** general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."

**Playbook:** specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Assessment: Reject paras 1.1 and 1.2.** Whole-data-room disclosure converts every document into a warranty qualification regardless of whether it fairly discloses the issue with sufficient detail. "Publicly searchable corporate records" is open-ended and unbounded. Require a disclosure standard of "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter," limited to the specific disclosures in section 2 onwards, with cross-referenced documents only.

Para 1.4 (no admission of anything) is standard but note it cuts against the Seller's own [STANDARD] characterisations – e.g. the Seller cannot simultaneously say the incident "is not expected to be material" and that nothing in the letter admits materiality either way.

---

## 5. Buyer knowledge exclusion (Clause 8.3)

**Seller:** no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Playbook:** delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

**Assessment: Reject.** This is the worst clause in the package. "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – it would bar claims on matters we did not actually know but could theoretically have found. Combined with whole-data-room disclosure (Item 4) it would make the warranties close to worthless. Delete entirely. If any knowledge concept is to survive, it should be (a) the Seller's knowledge, defined by named individuals after due enquiry, used to qualify specific warranties; and (b) expressly inapplicable to title, capacity, fraud and the specific indemnities.

---

## 6. Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3; Disclosure para 2)

**Seller:** reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

**Playbook:** effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours insufficient for a material customer.

**Assessment: Reject.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue – it is the single largest commercial exposure. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that as at 22 September no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions are in the data room. "Satisfied on delivery" means a conditional or qualified consent would satisfy the CP even if the 11.3 conditions are never met. Require: (a) a condition precedent that an unconditional written consent has been obtained **and** the 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied; (b) a Seller obligation of "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a Buyer walk-right and no deemed satisfaction; (c) a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within an agreed period post-Completion by reason of the change of control.

---

## 7. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7; Disclosure para 3)

**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."

**Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

**Assessment: Reject.** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means we acquire a company whose assets remain secured for an unquantified period, with the repayment mechanics entirely in the Seller's hands. The Disclosure Letter confirms no repayment and no discharge. Require a payout letter dated within 2 business days of Completion, repayment direct from the purchase price in the funds flow, and executed PPSR/security discharges (or an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt) delivered at Completion. Anything less needs Amelia Frost sign-off, which has not been sought.

---

## 8. Employee bonuses – DD-005 (Funds flow; Disclosure para 5)

**Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.

**Playbook:** must be a specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Assessment: Reject as drafted.** "A matter for the Seller" is ambiguous – it does not say the Seller will fund them. Because the bonuses are conditional on Completion, the liability will crystallise in the Company at the moment we own it. Unless deducted from price or paid by the Seller, we pay them. The Disclosure Letter also flags that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed; a realistic gross figure is above AUD 420k. Require either (a) a specific funds-flow line deducting the bonus amount plus on-costs from the price, or (b) a Seller covenant to pay with a specific indemnity (outside caps, basket and de minimis).

---

## 9. Ironquay IP – SOW3 (Clause 11.1; Disclosure para 4)

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate."

**Playbook:** broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way.

**Assessment: Broaden.** The real risk is not the AUD 180k fee – it is that under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every fee is paid. Until then the Company may not own IP it is using. An indemnity covering only the fee does not cover (a) loss if Ironquay disputes ownership, (b) costs of any confirmatory assignment, or (c) business loss from inability to use the materials. Require: Seller to procure payment and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion as a deliverable (preserving the cure), plus an indemnity covering all loss arising from any failure of title to the SOW3 materials. We should obtain bank confirmation of the AUD 180k position ourselves rather than relying on DD-010.

---

## 10. Export/privacy incident – DD-006 (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure para 6)

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."

**Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.

**Assessment: Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, but do not overclaim either.** The facts are that ~1,240 records went to an unintended external address and nobody yet knows whether the file was accessed or whether notification is required. That is exactly the state in which materiality cannot be assessed. Require: (a) a covenant to preserve all logs and complete a documented investigation before Completion; (b) a Completion deliverable summarising findings; (c) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general cap; (d) a bring-down obligation to update the disclosure. We should not at this stage assert a breach or a loss figure.

---

## 11. Sandbar supplier renewals (Disclosure para 8)

**Seller:** AUD 330k aggregate is ordinary-course operating cost.

**Playbook:** assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Assessment: Open – ask questions, do not fight yet.** The Disclosure Letter itself says it is not stated whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course – so the Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own disclosure. Request the three agreements, renewal dates, termination rights, and confirmation of whether any amount is accrued as at the Locked Box/Completion date. Treatment (working capital, debt-like item or nothing) follows from the answers.

---

## 12. Tax / IP warranties

**Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."

**Playbook:** OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed.

**Assessment: Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Nothing is settled. Tax and IP need their own schedules with their own caps and periods (tax typically running to the expiry of the relevant assessment period). Do not accept their collapse into the 18-month / 20% general regime via the Clause 12.3 default rule. We are not seeking unlimited liability; we are seeking a separate, longer regime.

---

## 13. Title evidence (Disclosure para 10)

**Seller:** title evidenced by the share register at DD-012.

**Playbook:** independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source.

**Assessment: Insufficient.** The share register is the Company's own document, supplied by the Seller. The Disclosure Letter candidly concedes it "does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification." Require: current ASIC company extract, PPSR search against the Company and the Seller, confirmation of no encumbrances over the shares, Seller board minutes/authority, and a title warranty backed by the fundamental regime in Item 2. This is a diligence action for us as much as a drafting point.

---

## 14. Items that appear acceptable / low priority

- **Office lease (DD-007):** notification only, not a consent. Confirm and ensure the notice is given at or before Completion. No push-back required beyond a covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** assignment restriction does not on its face trigger on a share sale. Confirm the clause has no change-of-control limb; if confirmed, no action.
- **Disclosure Letter paras 2–10 (specific disclosures):** these are factually candid and in several places undercut the Seller's own "[STANDARD]" framing. They are useful to us. Keep them; the problem is paras 1.1–1.2, not the specifics.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Threshold response:** Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and all [STANDARD] designations in writing. Confirm nothing is agreed.

**Must-fix (deal-protective, no authority to concede):**
1. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m; de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k first-dollar; 24-month period.
2. Separate fundamental/title regime – 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
3. Express unwaivable fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from everything.
4. Reverse the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/covenant categories separate.
5. Delete Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.
6. Replace whole-data-room / public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.
7. Bluefen: effective consent + evidence of 11.3 conditions as a CP; no deemed satisfaction.
8. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion.
9. DD-005 bonuses + on-costs: specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded with indemnity.

**Should-fix:**
10. Broaden Ironquay indemnity to cover failure of title to SOW3 materials; pre-Completion payment + confirmatory assignment as deliverable.
11. DD-006 incident: preservation, investigation, bring-down and specific indemnity – without asserting breach or quantum.
12. Separate Tax and IP regimes; reject "settled."
13. Independent title evidence (ASIC, PPSR, authority).

**Investigate:**
14. Sandbar renewals – information request before any price position.
15. Lease and Mossvale – confirm and close out.

**Internal actions:** No approach should be made to Amelia Frost for fallback authority at this stage – the Seller's package is sufficiently far from the playbook that the first counter should be at our opening positions across the board.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms that as at 22 September no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of the clause 11.3 conditions are in the data room. "Satisfied on delivery" means a conditional or qualified consent would satisfy the CP even if the 11.3 conditions are never met. Require: (a) a condition precedent that an unconditional written consent has been obtained **and** the 11.3 conditions evidenced as satisfied; (b) a Seller obligation of "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with a Buyer walk-right and no deemed satisfaction; (c) a specific indemnity if Bluefen terminates or re-prices within an agreed period post-Completion by reason of the change of control.

## 7. Riverlark facility (Clauses 2 / 7; Disclosure para 3)

**Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion."

**Playbook:** current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion; post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

**Assessment: Reject.** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means we acquire a company whose assets remain secured for an unquantified period, with the repayment mechanics entirely in the Seller's hands. The Disclosure Letter confirms no repayment and no discharge. Require a payout letter dated within 2 business days of Completion, repayment direct from the purchase price in the funds flow, and executed PPSR/security discharges (or an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt) delivered at Completion. Anything less needs Amelia Frost sign-off, which has not been sought.

## 8. Employee bonuses – DD-005 (Funds flow; Disclosure para 5)

**Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.

**Playbook:** must be a specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude them.

**Assessment: Reject as drafted.** "A matter for the Seller" is ambiguous – it does not say the Seller will fund them. Because the bonuses are conditional on Completion, the liability will crystallise in the Company at the moment we own it. Unless deducted from price or paid by the Seller, we pay them. The Disclosure Letter also flags that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are not addressed; a realistic gross figure is above AUD 420k. Require either (a) a specific funds-flow line deducting the bonus amount plus on-costs from the price, or (b) a Seller covenant to pay with a specific indemnity (outside caps, basket and de minimis).

## 9. Ironquay IP – SOW3 (Clause 11.1; Disclosure para 4)

**Seller:** indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate."

**Playbook:** broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified either way.

**Assessment: Broaden.** The real risk is not the AUD 180k fee – it is that under DD-004 clause 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until every fee is paid. Until then the Company may not own IP it is using. An indemnity covering only the fee does not cover (a) loss if Ironquay disputes ownership, (b) costs of any confirmatory assignment, or (c) business loss from inability to use the materials. Require: Seller to procure payment and a confirmatory assignment pre-Completion as a deliverable (preserving the cure), plus an indemnity covering all loss arising from any failure of title to the SOW3 materials. We should obtain bank confirmation of the AUD 180k position ourselves rather than relying on DD-010.

## 10. Export/privacy incident – DD-006 (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; Disclosure para 6)

**Seller:** "preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material."

**Playbook:** preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.

**Assessment: Do not accept the Seller's characterisation, but do not overclaim either.** The facts are that ~1,240 records went to an unintended external address and nobody yet knows whether the file was accessed or whether notification is required. That is exactly the state in which materiality cannot be assessed. Require: (a) a covenant to preserve all logs and complete a documented investigation before Completion; (b) a Completion deliverable summarising findings; (c) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), outside the general cap; (d) a bring-down obligation to update the disclosure. We should not at this stage assert a breach or a loss figure.

## 12. Tax / IP warranties

**Seller:** "settled under the general regime above."

**Playbook:** OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed.

**Assessment: Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Nothing is settled. Tax and IP need their own schedules with their own caps and periods (tax typically running to the expiry of the relevant assessment period). Do not accept their collapse into the 18-month / 20% general regime via the Clause 12.3 default rule. We are not seeking unlimited liability; we are seeking a separate, longer regime.

## Summary of recommendations

**Threshold response:** Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" and all [STANDARD] designations in writing. Confirm nothing is agreed.

**Must-fix (deal-protective, no authority to concede):**
1. Cap 25% / AUD 6.0m; de minimis AUD 5k; basket AUD 50k first-dollar; 24-month period.
2. Separate fundamental/title regime – 100% cap, 6+ years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge.
3. Express unwaivable fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from everything.
4. Reverse the "all Claims unless stated otherwise" default; keep Title/Tax/IP/indemnity/covenant categories separate.
5. Delete Clause 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion.
6. Replace whole-data-room / public-register disclosure with specific fair disclosure.
7. Bluefen: effective consent + evidence of 11.3 conditions as a CP; no deemed satisfaction.
8. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, security releases at Completion.
9. DD-005 bonuses + on-costs: specific funds-flow line or Seller-funded with indemnity.

**Should-fix:**
10. Broaden Ironquay indemnity to cover failure of title to SOW3 materials; pre-Completion payment + confirmatory assignment as deliverable.
11. DD-006 incident: preservation, investigation, bring-down and specific indemnity – without asserting breach or quantum.
12. Separate Tax and IP regimes; reject "settled."
13. Independent title evidence (ASIC, PPSR, authority).

**Investigate:**
14. Sandbar renewals – information request before any price position.
15. Lease and Mossvale – confirm and close out.

**Internal actions:** No approach should be made to Amelia Frost for fallback authority at this stage – the Seller's package is sufficiently far from the playbook that the first counter should be at our opening positions across the board.
